idea-plugin.name: VegaDuta
idea-plugin.description:
VegaDuta brings AI help into your IDE: chat about your code, review your uncommitted changes, draft commit messages, write tests and docs, and run a coding agent on your project. Use it with a VegaDuta account, or completely free with a model server you run on your own machine.

What you can do

  • Chat with context. The VegaDuta tool window (right-hand side) streams answers from your VegaDuta agents. Attach the current file, your selection, your uncommitted changes (diff), the current file's problems or your last 30 commits with one click. Each attachment is capped at 24,000 characters and marked when it was cut.
  • Jump to the code. When an answer points at lines in a project file, the plugin opens the file and selects them. Paths outside the project are refused.
  • Team knowledge search. Signed in, the chat can search your organisation's VegaDuta knowledge base.
  • Review My Changes. Sends your uncommitted diff for a review: real problems first, with file and line.
  • Generate Commit Message. Also on the toolbar above the commit message box. When you pick Use as commit message on the answer, the plugin fills in the box. It never commits for you.
  • Write Tests for Selection, Add Docs to Selection, Explain Selection and Refactor Selection from the editor's right-click menu.
  • Use the answer. Insert code at the cursor (replacing the selection, if there is one), open it in a new scratch file, or copy it.
  • Start a Coding Task. A multi-step agent that reads, searches, edits and runs commands in your open project. It asks before every edit and every command, and Ctrl+Z undoes its edits.
  • Run Workflow. Start one of your VegaDuta workflows and watch its progress.

Free and private: your own model server

You don't need an account. The quickest way: open Settings | Tools | VegaDuta, pick a model under Bundled on-device model and click Download & run. The plugin downloads the open-source llama.cpp server and a Qwen2.5 Coder model (about 1.1 GB for the recommended one), checks both files against pinned checksums, and runs the server on your computer. It starts again by itself the next time you open the IDE. Or use a server you already run (Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp) and click Detect local server. Either way you get:

  • Code completions from your model. Tick the box in Settings, then invoke basic completion twice (Ctrl+Space twice on Windows and Linux).
  • Start a Coding Task, which uses your model, or a provider you hold a key for. The model must support tool calling (for example qwen2.5-coder, llama3.1 or devstral).
  • On-device chat in the tool window. The one-click actions above work signed out too, and every turn goes only to the server you configured.

JetBrains' built-in browser has no WebGPU, so models never run inside the chat panel itself. "Local" always means a model server on your computer: the bundled one, or one you started yourself.

Private Mode

Turn it on in the chat panel or in Settings | Tools | VegaDuta. While it is on, no prompt, code, attachment or search query leaves your machine: hosted chat, knowledge search, the code sandbox, workflow runs and a coding agent pointed at a hosted provider are blocked by the IDE before any request is made. Your own local model server still works. Signing in and listing your agents and workflows still reach VegaDuta; they carry none of your content.

Sign in (for hosted agents and workflows)

Choose Tools | VegaDuta | Sign In… and approve the code in your browser. No local ports are opened, so it also works over Remote Development and SSH. Your session is kept in the operating system's keychain. For headless use, you can instead paste a scoped vmcp_ API key from your administrator.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.5.0

  • Free on-device AI, one click, no Ollama needed. Pick a model (Qwen2.5 Coder 1.5B, 3B or 7B) and VegaDuta downloads it, verifies its checksum and runs it on your machine with the bundled llama.cpp server. Chat, code completion and the coding agent then work offline and free, and it starts by itself next time. From the chat's "On-device" chip, or Settings > Tools > VegaDuta.

0.4.3

  • Fixed: the VegaDuta Agent tool window was an empty black panel until the first run. It now explains what the coding agent does and what it needs, with Start a coding task and Set up your model links and a start button in its title bar.
  • Fixed: "On-device off" in the chat was a dead end. It now reads "On-device: set up" and opens step-by-step setup for a free local model (Ollama or LM Studio, then Settings > Tools > VegaDuta).

0.4.1

  • Calmer, softer colours and gentler animation.
  • Panels no longer cut each other off: one drawer at a time, and the header, account bar and message box always stay visible.
  • A small tool window arranges itself properly and offers Open in window to give VegaDūta its own resizable window.
  • Recipes picked before sign-in are held and run once you sign in.

0.4.0

  • A redesigned tool window with VegaDūta's own colours, real buttons and an aligned sign-in bar. It follows the IDE's light or dark theme.
  • Always listening: the message box never locks. A question asked before you sign in is held and sent as soon as you do.
  • A home screen with quick starts, "Try asking" prompts and recipes for your role, available before sign-in.
  • Instant tools: 18 offline utilities (JSON, JWT, regex, cron, timestamps, test data, diff, hashes, Base64, UUIDs and more) that run inside the tool window with no account and nothing sent anywhere.

0.3.1

  • Fixed: sign-in failed when the sign-in server rate-limited the browser-approval check (HTTP 429). It now waits longer and keeps going until the code expires, instead of giving up.

0.3.0

  • Context attachments in chat: the current file, your selection, your uncommitted diff (from any VCS the IDE manages, or git diff HEAD when none is set up) and the current file's problems. Each attachment is capped at 24,000 characters and marked when cut. Anything the IDE can't supply, such as "nothing is selected", shows the reason instead of an empty attachment.
  • New actions in Tools | VegaDuta and the editor's right-click menu: Review My Changes, Generate Commit Message, Write Tests for Selection and Add Docs to Selection. They work signed in, and signed out with your own model server.
  • Generate Commit Message with VegaDuta in the commit message toolbar. Use as commit message fills in that box. If the box isn't available, the message is copied to the clipboard and a notification tells you.
  • Open in new file opens an answer in a scratch file. Insert now replaces the selection, if there is one. With no editor open, or a read-only file, it copies the code and tells you, instead of doing nothing.
  • The tool window gets its settings before it handles an action, so an action that opens the window for the first time no longer arrives too early.
  • Recent commits attachment: the last 30 commits (hash, date, author name, subject and body, no e-mail addresses) from git log, for commit messages in your team's style, release notes and standups.
  • Jump to the code: answers that point at lines in a project file open it with those lines selected. Paths outside the project folder, including through symbolic links, are refused.
  • Team knowledge search for signed-in users (not API keys). The search runs from the IDE; the chat page never holds your token.
  • Private Mode, in the chat panel and in Settings, remembered across restarts: no prompt, code, attachment or search query leaves your machine. Hosted chat, knowledge search, the code sandbox, workflow runs and a non-local coding-agent endpoint are blocked; your own local model server still works.

0.2.1

  • Fixed: multi-line replies lost every newline. One backend chunk is one SSE event, not one line - the reader now rejoins an event's data lines. Worst on the Planned / Careful / Rigorous reasoning depths, where the whole answer is a single event.

0.2.0

  • Start a Coding Task: a multi-step agent that reads, searches, edits and runs commands in the open project against your own OpenAI-compatible server. Edits go through the IDE's undo stack; every edit and every command asks first.
  • Local inference for the first time: code completions from an Ollama / LM Studio / llama.cpp server you run, configured under Settings | Tools | VegaDuta. No account needed.
  • Fixed: multi-line agent replies (Planned / Careful / Rigorous reasoning depths) arrived with every newline stripped.

0.1.0

  • Initial release: agent chat, workflow runs, explain/refactor selection.
